quest.title: Vimana Agama: First Chapter
quest.description: You heard from Araja that the Aranara were investigating a suspicious Nara near Devantaka Mountain. You wonder if it has anything to do with the missing kids at Vimara Village...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ahh! Nara...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't be afraid, we're not bad Nara! Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. You're Ararycan, right?

choices.text: We are friends of Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Araja sent us here, saying that you could help us.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Wah... there's been strange Nara around, that's why I was a bit scared.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We didn't mean to scare you! It's just that we didn't know you were so absorbed in...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Mmm... Since you can see Ararycan and are friends with Araja, the forest must recognize you. You can't be bad Nara.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Mm-hmm. You are good Nara. Ararycan is not afraid. Did you say that you have questions for Ararycan?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's right...

choices.text: We would like to know more about the delicious fungus.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: About that, Arachatora might know better than me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that's not what we were trying to ask! Have you seen some suspicious Nara around Vimara Village, Ararycan?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Ararycan what happened in brief.\n...Though how much Ararycan understood is a different story.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Arana is good Aranara. Protecting Vana often, and helping little Nara always, are what Arana does.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan once helped little Nara. Arana said that Marana's Avatar is taking little Nara away. So Ararycan helped.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Recently, the local Vana... Ah, I meant the forest. The forest and stream are always crying. Maybe, it's because of Marana. Marana, bad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Marana refers to the Withering, and Vana... That's gotta mean the forest. Well, that's some new Aranara words learned. Wait, does the forest cry, too?

choices.text: Maybe it's a figure of speech.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Sunshine brings happiness, but too much sunshine means less water. Water makes us grow, and no water means withering.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Songs bring happiness and power, getting sick makes us upset, and being sick for too long means withering. It's the same for Vana and Aranara.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ah, but Mint is different. Mint, so strong.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: The forest has been crying harder lately, Ararycan is worried.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it because Marana is harming the forest?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan is not sure. It smells like Marana, but not really the same. But Ararycan knows that, some bad dirty stuff are making the forest sick, in places Ararycan can't see.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: If the forest keeps being sick like this, a super giant Marana will come and suck all living things away! All the flowers will wither and leaves will fall.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: The fruits will go bad, and the mushrooms will stop growing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? No more mushrooms!? That means no more Chicken-Mushroom Skewers!

choices.text: We'll help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're here to help!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: And, around the area of "sickness," there is a weird Nara. That might be the bad Nara you want. Good Nara help Ararycan, and Ararycan takes you to him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Looks like we can help each other! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's exactly what I'm thinking.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Thank you. But, Marana is scary. Nara will die.

choices.text: We've dealt with that before. It'll be alright.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} defeated Marana before? You're very strong.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: And you are Golden Nara, just like the legendary Nara Varuna. You look reliable, I believe in you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmhmm. Just leave it to us! Now, we've got another question...

choices.text: About our reward...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Re... war? Do you mean enemies, Nara {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, come on, don't say such things to Aranara!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ararycan, do you know anything about the bad dirty stuff?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: I have seen many weird Hilinara with filthy stains on them. They've been acting suspiciously around the giant iron mountain.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hilinara...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Giant iron mountain? You mean that super big Ruin Guard over there? Speaking of which, something seems off with that ruin machine...

choices.text: It has no "eye"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, that's true! Other ruin machines all have a core that looks like an eye!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows nothing about ruin machines. As for the giant iron mountain, it has been here since a long, long time ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A long, long time... How long is that, exactly?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: The time it takes for a tiny little seed to grow into a giant tree that can touch the sky!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that sure is a long, long time. Well, it shouldn't be hurting the forest if it has been here for that long...

choices.text: Bad people might come here because of it, though.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm, you have a point. Bad guys like the Fatui, Treasure Hoarders and the Abyss Order! Super bad guys!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Bad Nara, bad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Either way, let's investigate it, shall we? Who knows, we might even find some treasure!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Thank you. Ararycan also saw that there are other strange things besides the suspicious Nara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then, let's go! Don't fall behind now, Ararycan!

choices.text: Who knows, it might revive itself at some point.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon hopes not.

choices.text: It has no core...
Tell me about the super bad, super dirty stuff...
Ooh, I don't wanna die!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on! We've dealt with that thing before, haven't we? With Rana and...

choices.text: We're here to look into the suspicious Nara.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows that. Around the area of "sickness," there is a weird Nara. That might be the bad Nara you want to find.

choices.text: Maybe it's something only Aranara could hear.
It cries very loudly...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Can Nara {NICKNAME} hear it, too? Nara {NICKNAME}, friend of forest.

choices.text: We'd like to know about the suspicious Nara around Vimara Village.
Araja sent us here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We've got some questions.

dialogues.text: Ah! How did you get up here?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, that's the suspicious Nara. He's been sneaking around here with that suspicious machine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmm, you're right. Coming to a place like this is pretty suspicious, alright...
Um, I'd say you're the suspicious ones here. After all, I am a certified researcher from the Akademiya, and you are outlanders of unknown origin.

choices.text: We've been commissioned to investigate this place.

response.text: Oh, a commission? So you're adventurers. Or perhaps you're Eremites or something?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Well, it doesn't matter. My name is Jazari, a Kshahrewar Researcher, as you can see. I don't care what you came here for, but don't get in the way of my research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's there to be researched in this deep cave?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: There are always things to be researched everywhere. As the saying goes, "ignorance is a researcher's disgrace."

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: You must have noticed the huge ruin machine out there, right? That is actually a Ruin Golem made in the ancient realm of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: In the local lexicon of Khaenri'ah, the name might possibly have been something like "Mechanical Warden."

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: See? We're right behind the Ruin Golem. The machine's operator, should there have been one, would have entered from here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... But a machine of this size would have required more than one operator, right?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Aha, that's among my research topics! Unfortunately, I haven't made much progress so far.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Exploring the Ruin Golem from the inside seems to be the only solution, and I am presently looking for a way in.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You sound more suspicious by the minute...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That's right, we did meet an Abyss Order member disguised as a researcher that one time! Paimon reckons he was called Enjou... {NICKNAME}, do you remember what happened to him again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We beat the snot out of him.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Hey, hey! Please don't! I'm a legitimate researcher...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Ugh, you don't believe me, do you... See this? This is an Investigation Charter from the Akademiya, with the highest possible level of clearance.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: That's not something to be given away on the streets. Certainly not one concerning investigations into ancient ruins as important as this. The Akademiya would never issue something like this casually.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I can't give you the original copy, but... Wait a second, where did I put my Kamera... I remember placing it inside my bag...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Be careful! He's taking that suspicious machine out again.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Jazari sets the device up carefully.\nIt is indeed a Kamera.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Is this the suspicious machine you mentioned? It's just a Kamera...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: A Kamera?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. It's a machine that takes pictures. It's pretty convenient!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Yes. This is a priceless item as far as the Akademiya is concerned. I can't just let you touch it... Wait. Who were you talking to just now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... about that...

choices.text: An imaginary friend...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Don't worry, I understand your condition. It's okay, we're friendly people here in Sumeru. You'll have no trouble making real friends. I guarantee it.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Still, do not get in the way of my research. After all, "nothing under the sun is truly new," and it is our duty as researchers to collect information and investigate it.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: All the charters are recorded in the Akademiya. If you are still skeptical, just keep an image of this for validation in the House of Daena.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Aaanyway, we've got something to discuss! {NICKNAME}, let's talk over there...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: As you wish.

choices.text: She's been alone since she was little...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Oh, so you often talk to yourself? Well, I've heard of similar cases before...

choices.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}, and I'm on the trail of a suspicious Nara.

response.text: Huh...? What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem! We've been commissioned to investigate the situation here.

dialogues.text: Ah! How did you get up here?

response.text: Huh...? What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem! We've been commissioned to investigate the situation here.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Some fate must have dictated that we would meet here. But that friend of yours... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: She must have led a lonely life. Be nice to her.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Anyway, I have to organize my findings. So, if you would excuse me...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Heh, finally believe me, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, guess you're not suspicious after all, Jazari.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We have some questions about the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Hehe, ask away. As a Kshahrewar researcher who specializes in studying ruin machines, I've been investigating this big guy over here for years.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: No one on this earth knows more about this Ruin Golem than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about beneath the earth, then?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Legends hold that the ancient realm of Khaenri'ah lies beneath the earth. Since they built all the ruin machines, it would be arrogant of me to say that I understand these devices better than they do.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about the "bad dirty stuff"...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Haha, you're looking for bad and dirty things, are you? Then you should visit the city.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: The city? Are bad things in the city?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

choices.text: This is just something adults say...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Anyway, this locale is somewhat polluted, which might be related to the "bad and dirty stuff" you mentioned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, here's the situation. We've heard that the forest here has...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You paraphrase Ararycan's words so that Jazari can understand them...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Is that so? Let me think about this... I might indeed have some clues.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: According to my research, all ruin mechanisms work on the same principle no matter what they do, whether it be flying or launching missiles...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: And well, a Ruin Golem is theoretically the same as a Ruin Guard, except that it was to be operated by people. Have you noticed anything abnormal about this Ruin Golem?

choices.text: It looks incredibly big.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Um, this isn't an issue of size. Have you not noticed that its core is missing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, this big guy here's got no peeper.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Exactly. According to the documents, ruin machines are powered by their cores. To be precise, by the dark power inside what you call an "eye."

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: When Khaenri'ah was destroyed, many ruin machines like this one burst out from the desert.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Although things are different now, even the Akademiya was unable to handle the cores back then.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: A single mistake could cause a core meltdown, leading to serious accidents. As a result, the Akademiya had no choice but to temporarily seal the cores and deal with them later.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: If the documents have it right, the core of this Ruin Golem should be sealed inside the ancient ruins known as "Dev's Cavern," which is right beneath our feet.

choices.text: Is there anything wrong with the core?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: There shouldn't be, but we have detected some energy leakage. The seal seems to have been damaged at some point, though we have no idea when.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Heh, the last time someone published a research report regarding such matters was more than ten years ago.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Any progress on this matter should warrant a large amount of funding from the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Funding? Are you saying that you get Mora from doing research?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: That's right. Speaking of which, we did talk about pollution a moment ago... For ecological topics, we might be able to file a subject application with Biol{RUBY#[S]Amurta}ogy.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: That would really be an archon-send for those who study fringe subjects like us.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: At first, I had planned on taking the route recorded in previous reports to look inside. Unexpectedly, all the entrances were blocked.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows. It's the place outside, where Ararycan sensed bad things.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I thought it might have been the Forest Watchers or the Vimara villagers who did it. But given what you described, someone must have sneaked inside and blocked the entrances.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Maybe it was the "Marana's Avatar" that you mentioned. Well, I wouldn't dare mess with something like that... Hilichurls are more than enough trouble for me, as you can see, or I wouldn't be stuck here right now.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: First things first, though. If you want to travel underground, I do have an idea as to how. Interested?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: This Nara, awesome! How do we travel beneath?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Guess you're pretty good after all. So, how do we get down there?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: We just need to find a way to enter this Ruin Golem and smash the blocked entrance open with it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Paimon just had a sense of déjà vu...

choices.text: That's my kind of plan!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: The data acquired from such an action would be priceless. Even if something goes wrong, the benefits still outweigh the risks.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Also, if we can investigate the core buried underground, I could... submit a funding application on your behalf.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: What do you think? That's killing two birds with one stone... Well, three birds, actually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #If we can get some funding... Let's help Jazari out, {NICKNAME}. Academic research is important too, after all!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Of course. But you'd best report to the Akademiya when you have the time, or this might be classified as malign research.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Anyway, let's try to get inside first. The operator might still be there. That would make for some great data... I mean, a good research subject...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It has been hundreds of years, you know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Never mind that. There might be treasure inside, right?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I'm quite sure that some antiques are stored within. Research on those would...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Since Mr. Jazari has put it like that, Paimon reckons we should do some... academic research!

choices.text: Great! So, how do we get in?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Aha! I almost forgot the most important thing. Opening the door to the Ruin Golem's cockpit requires an Amiti Device. To put it simply, a key.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: The bad news is that I don't have this key... But the good news is that I have discovered its whereabouts from studying the documents on hand.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: If you must know, I have scoured half the House of Daena for the few records available. The last report on the Amiti Device was published decades ago.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: And though I have now figured it all out, my findings cannot be published as things stand. Most irritating indeed...

choices.text: So where exactly is this key?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Ah, to put it simply, the key may be found in Port Ormos to the south, in the hands of an antique dealer named Royinjan. Could you please accompany me there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've been staying here doing research for so long, and you've never thought about visiting him?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Um, the thing is, I'm not good at dealing with merchants... They just don't understand me, which makes communication almost impossible.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I've been cheated out of a lot of Mora before on account of this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's true, I do find it hard to follow your thoughts at times, too.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: ...Wait, so this is actually all my fault? Agh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, whatever the case, we're going to Port Ormos, right? Let's go check it out, then.

choices.text: Why can't you publish your results?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: It's because those big shots don't see the academic value in this.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: But isn't "academic value" just pompous human evaluation, where they reduce knowledge down to mere practical tools?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Knowledge itself cannot be determined to be more or less valuable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, uh... Where exactly is this key? You haven't mentioned it yet...

choices.text: So how do we get in?
Are you serious...?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Mm? Well, it sounds like a good idea to me. It should be alright, and the data acquired from this would be priceless. Even if something does go wrong, the benefits still outweigh the risks.

choices.text: Let's cut this conversation short, shall we?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: *cough*... Anyway, the abnormality you sensed may have been pollution caused by the energy leakage from this core.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: But as you can see, someone has blocked the entrance.

choices.text: Its eye seems to be missing.
Don't think too much about it...

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Paimon needs friends? Ararycan could be your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Me too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Thanks, you two, but that's not the problem!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The issue is that he can't see you, Ararycan.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. When Nara grow up, they can't really see Aranara anymore. Young Nara see us because they are innocent. But grown Nara can't.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is a dreamer, favored by trees and flowers, so you can still see us, even as a grown-up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, we should be more careful when talking to Aranara in front of others...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon doesn't think Jazari was lying, anyway. You might have misunderstood him, Ararycan.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ararycan saw that Nara taking out his... Kamera, and doing *ka-chick* to hilinara. Very suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: If that Nara isn't bad... Ah, he runs away every time the hilinara come. So he can't really be friends with the hilinara.

choices.text: That sounds kinda sad.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Mm-hmm, the Nara holds his machine and runs so fast.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So he shouldn't be a bad person. Nor should he be related to the children at Vimara Village...

choices.text: I'm not particularly interested in all this, but we'll finish what we started.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, Paimon totally agrees!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, since he's doing research around here, he should be pretty familiar with the situation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe he can help you, Ararycan!

choices.text: I'm curious about the giant machine, actually.
He must be quite the runner, then.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Heh, finally believe me, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, guess you're not suspicious after all, Jazari.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We have some questions about the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Hehe, ask away. As a Kshahrewar researcher who specializes in studying ruin machines, I've been investigating this big guy over here for years.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: No one on this earth knows more about this Ruin Golem than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about beneath the earth, then?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Legends hold that the ancient realm of Khaenri'ah lies beneath the earth. Since they built all the ruin machines, it would be arrogant of me to say that I understand these devices better than they do.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about the "bad dirty stuff"...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Haha, you're looking for bad and dirty things, are you? Then you should visit the city.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: The city? Are bad things in the city?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

choices.text: This is just something adults say...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Anyway, this locale is somewhat polluted, which might be related to the "bad and dirty stuff" you mentioned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, here's the situation. We've heard that the forest here has...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You paraphrase Ararycan's words so that Jazari can understand them...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Is that so? Let me think about this... I might indeed have some clues.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: According to my research, all ruin mechanisms work on the same principle no matter what they do, whether it be flying or launching missiles...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: And well, a Ruin Golem is theoretically the same as a Ruin Guard, except that it was to be operated by people. Have you noticed anything abnormal about this Ruin Golem?

choices.text: It looks incredibly big.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Um, this isn't an issue of size. Have you not noticed that its core is missing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, this big guy here's got no peeper.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Exactly. According to the documents, ruin machines are powered by their cores. To be precise, by the dark power inside what you call an "eye."

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: When Khaenri'ah was destroyed, many ruin machines like this one burst out from the desert.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Although things are different now, even the Akademiya was unable to handle the cores back then.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: A single mistake could cause a core meltdown, leading to serious accidents. As a result, the Akademiya had no choice but to temporarily seal the cores and deal with them later.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: If the documents have it right, the core of this Ruin Golem should be sealed inside the ancient ruins known as "Dev's Cavern," which is right beneath our feet.

choices.text: Is there anything wrong with the core?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: There shouldn't be, but we have detected some energy leakage. The seal seems to have been damaged at some point, though we have no idea when.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Heh, the last time someone published a research report regarding such matters was more than ten years ago.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Any progress on this matter should warrant a large amount of funding from the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Funding? Are you saying that you get Mora from doing research?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: That's right. Speaking of which, we did talk about pollution a moment ago... For ecological topics, we might be able to file a subject application with Biol{RUBY#[S]Amurta}ogy.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: That would really be an archon-send for those who study fringe subjects like us.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: At first, I had planned on taking the route recorded in previous reports to look inside. Unexpectedly, all the entrances were blocked.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows. It's the place outside, where Ararycan sensed bad things.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I thought it might have been the Forest Watchers or the Vimara villagers who did it. But given what you described, someone must have sneaked inside and blocked the entrances.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Maybe it was the "Marana's Avatar" that you mentioned. Well, I wouldn't dare mess with something like that... Hilichurls are more than enough trouble for me, as you can see, or I wouldn't be stuck here right now.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: First things first, though. If you want to travel underground, I do have an idea as to how. Interested?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: This Nara, awesome! How do we travel beneath?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Guess you're pretty good after all. So, how do we get down there?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: We just need to find a way to enter this Ruin Golem and smash the blocked entrance open with it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is... is that even possible?

choices.text: That's my kind of plan!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: The data acquired from such an action would be priceless. Even if something goes wrong, the benefits still outweigh the risks.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Also, if we can investigate the core buried underground, I could... submit a funding application on your behalf.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: What do you think? That's killing two birds with one stone... Well, three birds, actually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #If we can get some funding... Let's help Jazari out, {NICKNAME}. Academic research is important too, after all!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Of course. But you'd best report to the Akademiya when you have the time, or this might be classified as malign research.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Anyway, let's try to get inside first. The operator might still be there. That would make for some great data... I mean, a good research subject...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It has been hundreds of years, you know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Never mind that. There might be treasure inside, right?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I'm quite sure that some antiques are stored within. Research on those would...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Since Mr. Jazari has put it like that, Paimon reckons we should do some... academic research!

choices.text: Great! So, how do we get in?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Aha! I almost forgot the most important thing. Opening the door to the Ruin Golem's cockpit requires an Amiti Device. To put it simply, a key.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: The bad news is that I don't have this key... But the good news is that I have discovered its whereabouts from studying the documents on hand.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: If you must know, I have scoured half the House of Daena for the few records available. The last report on the Amiti Device was published decades ago.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: And though I have now figured it all out, my findings cannot be published as things stand. Most irritating indeed...

choices.text: So where exactly is this key?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Ah, to put it simply, the key may be found in Port Ormos to the south, in the hands of an antique dealer named Royinjan. Could you please accompany me there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've been staying here doing research for so long, and you've never thought about visiting him?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Um, the thing is, I'm not good at dealing with merchants... They just don't understand me, which makes communication almost impossible.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I've been cheated out of a lot of Mora before on account of this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's true, I do find it hard to follow your thoughts at times, too.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: ... Wait, so this is actually all my fault? Agh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, whatever the case, we're going to Port Ormos, right? Let's go check it out, then.

choices.text: Why can't you publish your results?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: It's because those big shots don't see the academic value in this.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: But isn't "academic value" just pompous human evaluation, where they reduce knowledge down to mere practical tools?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Knowledge itself cannot be determined to be more or less valuable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, uh... Where exactly is this key? You haven't mentioned it yet...

choices.text: So how do we get in?
Are you serious...?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Mm? Well, it sounds like a good idea to me. It should be alright, and the data acquired from this would be priceless. Even if something does go wrong, the benefits still outweigh the risks.

choices.text: Let's cut this conversation short, shall we?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: *cough*... Anyway, the abnormality you sensed may have been pollution caused by the energy leakage from this core.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: But as you can see, someone has blocked the entrance.

choices.text: Its eye seems to be missing.
Don't think too much about it...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: This price... Did you come all the way here to make fun of me?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Well, you have a deal! I mean, Mora does come after friendship for us dealers, so I'll do you three a friendly favor today. There, I'll sell you the antique at the price you've named.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: *sob* My funding...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, here's the remaining funding...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Hmm, wait. What is this?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Isn't this just a normal Chaos Core!?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Nonsense. That's no ordinary Chaos Core, but the core of a Ruin Guard prototype found in Stormterror's Lair.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: See the marks left by the Great Wolf King of the North? This is a unique treasure alright, and no mistake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Then isn't this the one we saw at Stormterror's Lair? Didn't Dain take it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one's got to be a fake!

choices.text: Antiques are sold for their stories.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Whoa, that's impressive understanding for someone your age.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but that's not the point!

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Well, I don't know about this Dain fellow, but I sure have heard of Stormterror's Lair. Anyway, if you have different insights about antiques, we could discuss them in private...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Whatever this is, it's definitely not the Amiti Device.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: What I'm looking for is a key that can open up the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: According to my research, it should be in the hands of your grandfather, Mr. Hasad, the Golden Adventurer.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Well, at least that was the case several decades ago...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Jazari describes the story of Mr. Hasad the Golden Adventurer as recorded in documents.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Oh, come on. You should have just said this earlier.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: You didn't exactly let me...

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Haha, but that really brings back memories. It's been so long since I last heard stories about my grandpa.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: When I was little, grandpa would often tell me stories of his adventures. I thought then that he was just bragging, but what do you know, he actually was that awesome.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Speaking of which, it is mostly because of him that I became an appraiser of antiques. All the stories about treasures were just so intriguing.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Still, the thing you spoke of is not here with me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You haven't sold it off, have you?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: I wish I did... But treasures don't stay where they don't belong, as they say. I mean, isn't that what happens in all treasure-hunting legends?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Well, Grandpa didn't care about any of that stuff, but according to him, that device engraved with ancient characters was lost during one of his adventures in some underground cave.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: That was a long story, one which he told me so many times. But... I can't remember a single word of it now.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Actually, I even planned a treasure hunt for it with some others back then. And as to whether we really found it again... Well, if we did, it should still be hidden in a secret base at Vimara Village.

choices.text: A secret base at Vimara Village?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Haha, I always went there to play when I was just a kid. You know how kids love their secret bases.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Could you please show us to the secret base? Perhaps we could find some clues there.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: So this thing is that important to you, huh? Still, I haven't been back for over ten years...

choices.text: It's an important matter pertaining to scientific research.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Alright. Since you bought something from me, I'll take you there. But try to manage your expectations, okay? I really can't remember what happened that long ago.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: We're counting on you either way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hooray! To the secret base we go!

choices.text: It's an important matter pertaining to Mora.
Did you grow up in Vimara Village, too?
Maybe he was deceived, too.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ahh! Nara...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't be afraid, we're not bad Nara! Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. You're Ararycan, right?

choices.text: We are friends of Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Araja sent us here, saying that you could help us.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Wah... There's been strange Nara around. That's why I was a bit scared.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We didn't mean to scare you! It's just that we didn't know you were so absorbed in...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Mmm... Since you can see Ararycan and are friends with Araja, the forest must recognize you. You can't be bad Nara.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Mm-hmm. You are good Nara. Ararycan is not afraid. Did you say that you have questions for Ararycan?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's right...

choices.text: We would like to know more about the delicious fungus.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: About that, Arachatora might know better than me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that's not what we were trying to ask! Have you seen any suspicious Nara around Vimara Village, Ararycan?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Ararycan what happened in brief.\n...Though how much Ararycan understood is a different story.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Arana is good Aranara. Protecting Vana often, and helping little Nara always, are what Arana does.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan once helped little Nara. Arana said that Marana's Avatar is taking little Nara away. So Ararycan helped.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Recently, the local Vana... Ah, I meant the forest. The forest and stream are always crying. Maybe, it's because of Marana. Marana, bad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Marana refers to the Withering, and Vana... That's gotta mean the forest. Well, that's some new Aranara words learned. Wait, does the forest cry, too?

choices.text: Maybe it's a figure of speech.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Sunshine brings happiness, but too much sunshine means less water. Water makes us grow, and no water means withering.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Songs bring happiness and power, getting sick makes us upset, and being sick for too long means withering. It's the same for Vana and Aranara.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ah, but Mint is different. Mint, so strong.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: The forest has been crying harder lately, Ararycan is worried.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it because Marana is harming the forest?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan is not sure. It smells like Marana, but not really the same. But Ararycan knows that some bad dirty stuff are making the forest sick, in places Ararycan can't see.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: If the forest keeps being sick like this, a super giant Marana will come around to suck all the living things away! All the flowers will wither, and all the leaves will fall.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: The fruits will go bad, and mushrooms will stop growing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? No more mushrooms!? That means no more Chicken-Mushroom Skewer!

choices.text: We'll help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're here to help!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: And around the area of "sickness," there is a weird Nara. That might be the bad Nara you want. Good Nara help Ararycan, and Ararycan takes you to him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Looks like we can help each other! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's exactly what I'm thinking.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Thank you. But, Marana is scary. Nara will die.

choices.text: We've dealt with that before. It'll be alright.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} defeated Marana before? You're very strong.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: And you are golden Nara, just like the legendary Nara Varuna. You look reliable, so I believe in you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmhmm. Just leave it to us! Now, we've got another question...

choices.text: About our reward...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Re... war? Do you mean enemies, Nara {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, come on, don't say such things to Aranara!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ararycan, do you know anything about the bad dirty stuff?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: I have seen many weird Hilinara with filthy stains on them. They've been acting suspiciously around the giant iron mountain.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hilinara...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Giant iron mountain? You mean that super big Ruin Guard over there? Speaking of which, didn't we see a similar machine earlier?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks it was called a Ruin Golem or something. But this big guy looks a little different...

choices.text: It has no "eye"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's true! The other Ruin Golem we've seen have a core that looks like an eye, just like Ruin Guards!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows nothing about any Ruin Golem. As for the giant iron mountain, it has been here, since a long, long time ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A long, long time... How long is that, exactly?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: The time it takes for a tiny little seed to grow into a giant tree that can touch the sky!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that sure is a long, long time. Well, it shouldn't be hurting the forest if it has been here for that long...

choices.text: Bad people might come here because of it, though.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm, you have a point. Bad guys like the Fatui, Treasure Hoarders and the Abyss Order! Super bad guys!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Bad Nara, bad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Either way, let's investigate it, shall we? Who knows, we might even find some treasure!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Thank you. Ararycan also saw that there are other strange things besides the suspicious Nara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then, let's go! Don't fall behind now, Ararycan!

choices.text: Who knows, it might revive itself at some point.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon hopes not.

choices.text: It has no core...
Tell me about the super bad, super dirty stuff...
Ooh, I don't wanna die!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on! We've dealt with that thing before, haven't we? With Rana and...

choices.text: We're here to look into the suspicious Nara...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows. Around the area of "sickness," there is a weird Nara. That might be the bad Nara you want.

choices.text: Maybe it's something only Aranara can hear.
It cries very loudly...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Can Nara {NICKNAME} hear it, too? Nara {NICKNAME}, friend of forest.

choices.text: We'd like to know about the suspicious Nara around Vimara Village.
Araja sent us here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We've got some questions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, here's the remaining funding...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Now, let me see... Wait, this is by no means the Amiti Device I spoke of.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: What I'm looking for is a key that can open up the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: According to my research, it should be in the hands of your grandfather, Mr. Hasad, the Golden Adventurer.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well, at least that was the case several decades ago...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jazari describes the story of Hasad the Golden Adventurer as stated by the documents.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Oh, come on. You should have just said this earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: You didn't exactly let me...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Haha, but that really brings back memories. It's been so long since I last heard stories about my grandpa.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: When I was little, grandpa would often tell me stories of his adventures. I thought then that he was just bragging, but what do you know, he actually was that awesome.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, it is mostly because of him that I became an appraiser of antiques. All the stories about treasures were just so intriguing.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Still, the thing you spoke of is not here with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? You haven't sold it off, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: I wish I did... But treasures don't stay where they don't belong, as they say. I mean, isn't that what happens in all treasure-hunting legends?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Well, Grandpa didn't care about any of that stuff, but according to him, that device engraved with ancient characters was lost during one of his adventures in some underground cave.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: That was a long story, one which he told me so many times. But... I can't remember a single word of it now.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Actually, I even planned a treasure hunt for it with some others back then. And as to whether we really found it again... Well, if we did, it should still be hidden in a secret base at Vimara Village.

choices.text: A secret base at Vimara Village?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Haha, I always went there to play when I was just a kid. You know how kids love their secret bases.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Could you please show us to the secret base? Perhaps we could find some clues there.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: So this thing is that important to you, huh? Still, I haven't been back for many years...

choices.text: It's an important matter pertaining to scientific research.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Alright. Since you bought something from me, I'll take you there. But do manage your expectations, okay? I really can't remember what happened that long ago.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: We're counting on you either way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hooray! To the secret base we go!

choices.text: It's an important matter pertaining to Mora.
Did you grow up in Vimara Village, too?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: I see how it is. You're not buying anything, are you? I didn't do decades of business here just to be messed with!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no, that's not what we meant...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: 500,000, that's the final deal!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... What are we gonna do, Jazari?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: *sob* I'll have to accept that for the sake of my research...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Welcome. You must be travelers from abroad. What brings you here to my shop? Would you like to make any purchases or seek to appraise any items?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're Royinjan, the antique dealer, right?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Royinjan, the Chief Antique Appraiser, to be precise. Did you come specifically to visit me? Well, I shan't let you down then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're looking for a certain antique.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Oh? Then you've come to the right place. If you can name it, Royinjan here can tell you about it.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: I've probably seen enough antiques to lay out across the entire marketplace. Even the Akademiya might not have seen quite as many.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're looking for the... Um, what's the thingy's name again? Paimon can't remember.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Hi, we're looking for an Amiti Device.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Eh? I've never heard of something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! You just said that we could name anything!

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Haha, don't worry. I haven't heard of that name, but I might yet know of the thing you want. Antiques tend to have a variety of monikers, you see.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Can you describe the thing that you're looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ugh, how should I put it? The documents didn't include a particularly detailed description...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: It's an item in the style of those ruin machines, and it should be an identification device of sorts.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: It should be marked with unique Khaenri'ah-style patterns, that can be recognized to be chronologically different from the common types seen on Ruin Guards, thus marking this as some sort of earlier version of the device...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: And considering what we know of ruin archaeology...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Ah, alright, you can stop now. I know what you're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ha, so you know? That's so very helpful, thank you. In that case, please give it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Uh, that's not how this works. This item is very precious. If you really want it, you'll have to pay for it. And that's... 500,000 Mora, at the very least.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: It's an antique, you know. What I'm offering is a pretty common price.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ugh... But what if the Mora we spend here can't guarantee a successful report...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Let's just help him out, shall we, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've helped others bargain before, haven't we? You're probably a dab hand by now.

choices.text: Well, not really.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Really? That's... a relief. I'm terrible at things like this.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: That's everything on me. Just take it. I'll have to find a gig with the Eremite over there if that's not sufficient, though.

choices.text: I'm good at dealing with merchants.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fine, I'll just make do with that amount. But treat the item well, okay? Each antique has many stories and emotions behind it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Pretty good, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Hmm, this price is a little too low... You know what I mean?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, that must be the "Ararycan" who was mentioned earlier, right? Let's go ask him!
